hinge.title: Classify an electric cell as a dry cell rather than a Voltaic cell from how its electrolyte is held and how convenient it is for everyday use.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: A dry cell is a Voltaic cell because both have two terminals and an electrolyte.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The decision still holds even if we ignore this condition: A dry cell is still an electric cell and includes parts such as a carbon rod, electrolyte, and zinc container.

intelligence.enrichment: A dry cell has an electrolyte that is not a free liquid, making it more convenient for everyday use than a Voltaic cell with a liquid electrolyte. electrolyte not present as a free liquid -> cell is easier to carry and use in everyday devices; liquid electrolyte in a Voltaic cell -> less convenient for everyday use The learner correctly applies this rule: A dry cell has an electrolyte that is not a free liquid, making it more convenient for everyday use than a Voltaic cell with a liquid electrolyte. A dry cell has no electrolyte at all because dry means completely dry inside.
